description: Open-source, agent-agnostic self-improving journaling harness. Core = preference container: it finds genuine questions, reaches out (note/email), ingests feedback, decides, supersedes rules, applies them, records usage receipts and audits itself weekly. Models: PAD, G, XP. Read docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md first. Python 3 stdlib only, package etrace. Quality check: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

userStories.title: Package scaffold and config loader
userStories.description: As a user, I configure the system with one trace.toml file.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/__init__.py, etrace/__main__.py, etrace/config.py exist

config.load(path) reads TOML via tomllib: timezone (default America/Chicago), data_dir, preset ('default' or 'tiger-method'), language ('zh'|'en'), task times for calibrate/feedback/daily/g/audit, outreach ('note' or 'note+email'), credential file paths for email and notion
Unknown keys raise a clear error naming the key; missing optional keys get defaults
examples/trace.toml documents every key
tests/test_config.py added
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Append-only JSONL store with locking
userStories.description: As the engine, I need storage that never loses or rewrites history.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/store.py: append(name, record), read_all(name), write_json_atomic(path, obj) via temp file + os.replace
A lock file prevents concurrent writers; stale locks older than a timeout are reported, never silently removed
append rejects records without 'id' and duplicate ids in the same file
Tests use tempfile directories only
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Journal file format and protected blocks
userStories.description: As a user, nothing I write is ever silently changed by the AI.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/journal.py parses/writes Markdown with <!-- trace:ai:NAME --> / <!-- trace:user:NAME --> / <!-- trace:verbatim --> markers as in docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md 4.4

new_note(date, preset, language) creates the next-day note with: empty G self-rating table (8 items), empty PAD self table (morning/noon/afternoon + other rows), journal zone, feedback zone, empty ai:questions block; empty cells stay empty
replace_ai_block(doc, name, text) only touches ai blocks; save() compares hashes of all user and verbatim blocks before vs after and raises ProtectedBlockChanged on any difference
Round-trip: parse then save of an unmodified file is byte-identical, including Chinese text and trailing spaces
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Container: rules with scoped supersession
userStories.description: As the system, the newest user instruction wins within the same scope.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/container/rules.py: add_rule(rule_id, scope, text, expressed_at, source_feedback_id), active_rules(), history(rule_id)
A rule with the same scope and later expressed_at supersedes the old one: the old one leaves active_rules() but stays in history with superseded_by and reason
expressed_at is the user's original expression time, not write time; an earlier-expressed rule added later does NOT supersede a newer one
Different scopes coexist; rules.json written atomically with a monotonically increasing version
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Container: feedback intake from notes
userStories.description: As a user, I give feedback by writing in my note.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/container/feedback.py: ingest_notes(journal_dir) reads every user:feedback block, splits entries by blank line, stores each new entry verbatim with id = note date + block + content hash, observed_at, refers_to_date, optional question_id if the entry starts with [Q-id]
Re-running does not duplicate; an edited entry becomes a new version linked to the previous one
Template placeholder text is never ingested
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Container: genuine questions
userStories.description: As the system, I ask only real, evidence-based questions.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/container/questions.py: add_question(...) requires source, date, evidence (quote or verifiable behavior), two candidate judgments, the uncertainty, affected dimensions, dedupe_key; missing any field raises
Same dedupe_key as an open or answered question is rejected; a still-open question can get at most one follow-up
Lifecycle open -> answered|skipped; answered requires feedback_id
daily_status(date) returns either the open questions or the exact text 'no new important questions' only if scan_ok=True; if scan failed it returns 'scan failed, cannot judge'
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Container: decisions, usage receipts, validation
userStories.description: As the system, I prove that feedback was actually applied.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/container/decisions.py: decide(feedback_ids, decision_text, value_source='user'|'agent_decision', rule_changes) appends to decisions.jsonl and applies rule changes via rules.py

etrace/container/usage.py: record(task, target, rule_version, feedback_ids, decision_ids, before, after, status) where status in changed|confirmed|no_match|not_applicable|blocked, and verified_readback must be True
etrace/container/validate.py: fails if an answered question lacks feedback_id, a decision lacks a source feedback, or a decision older than 2 days has no usage receipt and is not listed as pending
Reading rules without a receipt never counts as applied (test)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Outreach: questions and decision report in the note
userStories.description: As a user, I see what the system wants to ask and what it decided.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/outreach/note.py writes the ai:questions block of today's note: numbered open questions with [Q-id] so I can reply in the feedback zone, then a decision report: one or two sentence summary, then per decision what/why/which feedback, ending with an invitation to say what I agree or disagree with
Records a notifications.jsonl entry only after reading the note back and finding the text
zh and en templates; output stays readable at phone width (no line over 120 chars in tests)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Presets: default and tiger-method, complete
userStories.description: As a new user, everything works on day one without configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: presets/default and presets/tiger-method each contain pad.json, g.json, xp.json, rules.json, question_templates.json with zh+en labels, matching docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md 4.2
pad.json: five levels per axis with anchors, 27-word table (see progress.txt), projection 1-2 low, 3 mid, 4-5 high
xp.json: six dims with caps 18,16,16,14,14,12 (names differ per preset), levels 0-4, ordinary cap 10, uncapped unique-id events; NO personal events anywhere
etrace/presets.py validates: weights per group sum to 1.0, exactly 27 word cells, positive caps, every rule has scope and text; invalid preset raises ValueError naming the field
presets/tiger-method/README.md explains how the XP dimensions were grown from real difficulties and how to grow your own
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: PAD core model
userStories.description: As the engine, I validate PAD points and summarize a day.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/models/pad.py: PadPoint(date, slot in early_morning|morning|noon|afternoon|evening|late_night or exact time, P/A/D floats 0-5, provenance self_report|model_inference, source, confidence low|medium|high, optional duration_hours, optional self_value)
model_inference points need source and confidence; self_value is kept unchanged when the AI value differs and a reason is required
project(p,a,d) returns the 27-table word; daily_summary is the per-axis duration-weighted mean, unknown durations equal-weighted and flagged
validate_day fails unless morning, noon and afternoon are all present
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: PAD SVG chart
userStories.description: As a user, I see my day's PAD trajectory in one consistent chart.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/chart.py pad_svg(points, kind='day'|'week'): canvas 1240x590, background #F3F5F7, y fixed 0-5, ticks 1-5, exactly three smooth solid lines P=#D6336C A=#F08C00 D=#1C7ED6 width 5, no dots or dashed lines
Gaussian-kernel local linear smoothing, bandwidth 2.5 h (day) / 0.75 d (week)
Slot-only points use fixed slot positions and the caption says positions are not exact clock times
Tests parse the SVG with xml.etree and check size, line count, colors
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: G score computation
userStories.description: As the engine, I compute B, E and G exactly.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/models/g.py compute(items, preset): weighted B and E, G=(B+E)/2, no early rounding, display rounds to 1 decimal
Group computed only if all 4 items exist; G only if B and E exist; otherwise None, never 0
Items need provenance, source, confidence; self-rated values are stored separately and preserved
legend(preset, language) returns the symbol explanation (formulas, item names, anchors, 'not a clinical scale')
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: G continuity gap fill
userStories.description: As the engine, I fill missing item scores transparently.
acceptanceCriteria: g.gap_fill fills only missing items in fixed order: linear interpolation between nearest real left/right values (historical_bridge), else carry forward (continuity_carry_forward), else 5.0 (scale_prior)
Filled items have confidence low, method, neighbor dates/values; day gets explicit_gap_fill=true
When a later real value appears, re-running creates a NEW revision replacing carry-forward with bridge; old revision kept
g.training_eligible(day) is False for gap-filled days
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Frozen predictions and calibration gate
userStories.description: As the engine, I learn from feedback without fooling myself.
acceptanceCriteria: g.predict appends an immutable snapshot (id, date, revision, rubric_version, items, created_at) to predictions.jsonl
g.feedback requires a prediction_id created before the feedback time, else rejects
Only numbers the user explicitly gave are training labels; text feedback is stored with targets={}
Numeric correction enabled only after 10 training days + 10 later test days show lower MAE than no correction; labels from other rubric versions are not mixed
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: XP scoring
userStories.description: As a user, daily XP reflects real growth and big moments are not flattened.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/models/xp.py score_day: dimension level 0-4, points = cap*level/4; ordinary clamped 0..10; events need unique event_id and occurred_on; no daily cap; integer total
An event_id already booked on another day is rejected
week_total sums displayed daily totals only, no weekly bonus; missing days reported as missing, never 0
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Outreach: email plugin
userStories.description: As a user, the system actively emails me questions and reads my replies.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/outreach/email.py sends via smtplib and reads replies via imaplib; credentials read from the file path in trace.toml, never logged
Before sending, checks notifications.jsonl to dedupe by date+kind; marks sent only after the message is found in the Sent folder via IMAP; otherwise failed/unknown with reason
Reply parsing: only messages sent to the user's address, after the question was sent, matching the subject tag; quoted older text and signatures are stripped; dedupe by message_id+question_id
Email body carries minimum context, never full journal text
Tests mock smtplib and imaplib; no network
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Weekly implementation audit
userStories.description: As the system, I check every week that I really applied what I learned.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/container/audit.py weekly(as_of) walks every chain in the last 7 days plus older open ones: question -> feedback -> decision -> rule -> usage receipt
Reports broken links, decisions with no receipt, receipts without verified_readback, and samples one applied and one not_applicable item
Writes audits/YYYY-Www.md and .json; returns pass only if there are zero broken chains; structural completeness alone is not a pass (test)
Explicit user approval and silence are reported separately
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Local git checkpoint
userStories.description: As a user, every change to my data is versioned privately.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/checkpoint.py: checkpoint(data_dir, message) initializes a local git repo if missing and commits only if there are changes (no empty commits)
Never pushes unless trace.toml sets a remote explicitly; never force-pushes
Tests run git in a temp dir and skip cleanly if git is unavailable
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: CLI
userStories.description: As a user or agent, I drive everything from one command.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -m etrace with: init --preset NAME, note new DATE, question add FILE, feedback ingest, decide FILE, usage add FILE, outreach send, pad add FILE, pad chart DATE, g predict FILE, g feedback FILE, g report, xp score FILE, audit weekly, checkpoint MSG, rules list, validate
init copies the chosen preset into a fresh data dir and creates today's note so the loop runs on day one
FILE commands accept agent JSON; bad input prints field-level errors and exits 2; validate exits 1 on any failure
tests/test_cli.py calls cli.main(argv) against a temp data dir
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Agent task prompts (zh/en)
userStories.description: As any coding agent, I get a short task prompt that defers rules to the engine.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/prompts/{zh,en}/ contain _principles.md (the 9 principles), calibrate.md, feedback.md, daily.md, g.md, audit.md
python3 -m etrace prompt TASK renders with values from trace.toml and active rules; no absolute paths or personal data
Every prompt: run checkpoint before and after, output JSON for the matching CLI command, run validate at the end, report failures honestly
Each rendered prompt is under 6000 characters (test)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Scheduler adapters
userStories.description: As a user, I install the schedule for my agent of choice.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -m etrace schedule --target codex|claude-code|cron --out DIR writes files but never installs them
codex: one automation.toml per task (kind=cron, rrule from trace.toml); cron: crontab snippet; claude-code: shell script using 'claude -p' with the rendered prompt
Tests check times and timezone match trace.toml for all five tasks
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Optional Notion output adapter
userStories.description: As a Notion user, I mirror my daily report into Notion.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/adapters/notion.py converts a journal file to Notion blocks and pushes via urllib with a token read from the file in trace.toml
Local Markdown stays the source of truth; Notion is never read back into user blocks
Tests mock HTTP; no network

userStories.title: Privacy guard, example persona, README
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I am sure no personal data ships and newcomers can start fast.
